items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Personal objectives"?
items.answer: The financial, social and higher-level needs of the people working in the organisation.

options: Survival, profit and growth of the organisation.
The financial, social and higher-level needs of the people working in the organisation.
Creating benefit for society, such as using environment-friendly methods and giving employment to disadvantaged sections.
The process of getting things done with the aim of achieving goals effectively and efficiently.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of effectiveness but not of efficiency?
items.answer: Meaning: completing the task on time (achieving the result)

items.stem: Explain the following characteristics of management: (i) Continuous process (ii) Dynamic function.
items.answer: (i) Continuous process: Planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling are performed continuously. (ii) Dynamic function: Management adapts the organisation to its changing environment.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling are performed continuously. (ii) Management adapts the organisation to its changing environment.

items.stem: Menon Traders, a hospital in Jaipur, a school run by an NGO and a government office all use management to run their work. Which characteristic of management is highlighted?
items.answer: All-pervasive
items.markingKey: (b) All-pervasive. Management is needed in all types of organisations.

items.stem: Mishra Brothers uses solar power and employs people with disabilities in its bicycles unit. Which objective of management is being pursued? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Social objectives. It creates benefits for society.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Social objectives; 2 marks for the justification: It creates benefits for society.

items.stem:
Verma Agencies, a organic food products maker in Pune, met its production target on time this year, but its costs were 20% higher than budgeted because of wastage.
(i) Was the management effective, efficient or both? Explain. (ii) Why should a manager aim at both?
items.answer: (i) Effective (target achieved on time) but not efficient (cost was higher than needed). (ii) Achieving the goal is not enough; resources must be used optimally to remain competitive.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Effective (target achieved on time) but not efficient (cost was higher than needed). (ii) Achieving the goal is not enough; resources must be used optimally to remain competitive.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the nature of management is correct?
items.answer: Management is all-pervasive.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Management is all-pervasive.
options: Management is needed only in profit-making organisations.
Management is needed only at the top level.
Management is a tangible force that can be seen.

items.stem: Management at Bansal Brothers covers work to be done, the people who do it and the operations of production. Which characteristic of management is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Multidimensional. It manages work, people and operations.

items.stem: Das Agencies wants to earn enough revenue to cover its costs and stay in business in a tough market. Which objective of management is being pursued?
items.answer: Organisational objectives

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Profession"?
items.answer: An occupation backed by specialised knowledge and training, with entry restricted by a professional body and a code of conduct.

items.answer: Motivating employees to achieve objectives
items.markingKey: (a) "Motivating employees to achieve objectives" is one of the functions of middle management, not one of the functions of top management.

items.stem: Which feature is being described? In each case give a reason. (i) A great deal of literature on motivation and leadership is available to Diya, a new manager at Patel Industries. (ii) Diya became a better manager after years of practice and creative problem solving at Patel Industries.
items.answer: (i) Existence of theoretical knowledge: Management has a body of theoretical knowledge. (ii) Based on practice and creativity: Skill grows with practice and creativity.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Existence of theoretical knowledge (ii) Based on practice and creativity

items.stem: Explain the following functions of supervisory management: (i) Maintaining quality of output (ii) Linking management and workers.
items.answer: (i) Maintaining quality of output: They ensure that work meets quality standards. (ii) Linking management and workers: They pass on the problems of workers to middle management.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) They ensure that work meets quality standards. (ii) They pass on the problems of workers to middle management.

items.stem: What is meant by "Supervisory management"?
items.answer: The foremen and supervisors who directly oversee the work of operative employees.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The foremen and supervisors who directly oversee the work of operative employees.

items.stem: Kulkarni and Sons pays competitive salaries and offers recognition and growth to its staff. Which objective of management is being pursued? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Personal objectives. It meets the financial and higher-level needs of employees.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Personal objectives; 2 marks for the justification: It meets the financial and higher-level needs of employees.

items.stem:
Mehta Agencies, a garments maker in Dehradun, met its production target on time this year, but its costs were 20% higher than budgeted because of wastage.
(i) Was the management effective, efficient or both? Explain. (ii) Why should a manager aim at both?
items.answer: (i) Effective (target achieved on time) but not efficient (cost was higher than needed). (ii) Achieving the goal is not enough; resources must be used optimally to remain competitive.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Effective (target achieved on time) but not efficient (cost was higher than needed). (ii) Achieving the goal is not enough; resources must be used optimally to remain competitive.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of top management but not of supervisory management?
items.answer: Position: senior-most executives
items.markingKey: (d) top management: Position: senior-most executives. The other options describe supervisory management.
options: Nature of work: routine and operational

items.stem: A great deal of literature on motivation and leadership is available to Meera, a new manager at Kapoor Retail. Which feature is being described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Existence of theoretical knowledge. Management has a body of theoretical knowledge.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Existence of theoretical knowledge; 2 marks for the justification: Management has a body of theoretical knowledge.

items.stem: What is meant by "Organising"?
items.answer: Assigning duties, grouping tasks, establishing authority and allocating resources required to carry out a plan.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Assigning duties, grouping tasks, establishing authority and allocating resources required to carry out a plan.
